description:
STATUS (2026-09-02, origin/main a3a9761d1): LIVE NATIVE WRONG ANSWER
for captured closures and native refusal for sequential body destructuring.
The old “compiles on no path” title and forwarding-hop requirement are stale:
interp is green, capture-free clause-head destructuring is green on all three
doors, and the minimal captured wrong answer needs no forwarding hop.

MINIMAL WRONG-ANSWER REPRO:

  fn apply_box({tag, f}, x), do: {tag, f.(x)}
  fn make(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  fn main(), do: dbg(apply_box({:a, make(1)}, 10))

Expected and interp:
  {:a, 11}

Current JIT and AOT both compile and exit 0, but print a run-dependent large
integer instead of 11 (examples observed at a3a9761d1:
936748776442904720 on JIT and 936748726879907056 on AOT). Do not pin those
numbers; they vary. The equivalent top-level callable control

  fn apply_fun(f, x), do: f.(x)
  fn make(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  fn main(), do: dbg(apply_fun(make(1), 10))

prints 11 on interp, JIT, and AOT, so nesting/projection is the trigger.

SECOND WITNESS — SEQUENTIAL BODY MATCH:

  fn apply_box(box, x) do
    {tag, f} = box
    {tag, f.(x)}
  end

With capture-free lambdas nested in the tuple, interp prints the correct values
but both native doors refuse. The two-target forwarding version currently says:

  native cannot project captures out of a callable that names no function
  native executable lowering failed

A single-target or direct-call spelling can refuse earlier with
“native attempted to materialize direct-only callable”. Replacing the body
match with the clause-head pattern makes the capture-free program green, so
the old claim that the pattern-destructured form fails all three doors is also
obsolete.

SIGNAL / FIRST VISIBLE CONTRADICTION:

For the captured minimal repro, the backend dump gives the projected field the
semantic type

  closure[make/1#lambda...](int)

but its transport layout is

  callable(<unknown>/0 captures=[] shapes=[] lanes=[])

and that value is then used by closure_call. The nested callable's concrete
construction/capture information has disappeared at the projection seam.
For the sequential body match, runtime demand changes the tuple input into a
structural atom lane plus the same zero-lane unknown callable; the source tuple
was a boxed ValueRef. Native's diagnostics in jobs/native.rs are backstops
exposing this contradiction, not the fix.

GOAL:

A callable projected from an aggregate must retain the runtime value,
construction identity, and recursively described capture transport required to
invoke it. Clause-head patterns and sequential matches must agree. Static
grounding may avoid runtime dispatch, but it must not erase the callable value
or its captures before native invocation.

REQUIRED WORK:

- Preserve concrete callable construction/capture transport through tuple field
  views and pattern bindings, using the same callable facts that make the
  top-level control correct.
- Make sequential tuple-match demand preserve a usable callable field instead
  of producing an absent zero-lane anonymous callable.
- Ensure native invocation reads the capture value actually minted by make/1;
  do not silence the current diagnostics or accept pointer-derived garbage.
- Add red-first behavior fixtures for:
  1. a captured closure projected by a clause-head tuple pattern, and
  2. a capture-free closure projected by a sequential body match.
  Include expected output and Elixir oracles.
- Promote the existing dispatch-layer claims to three-door coverage and remove
  the stale fz-kdt.137 “fixture cannot be written” caveat from
  callsite_dispatch.rs and dispatch-matrix documentation.

ACCEPTANCE / CHECKS:

- Both new fixtures print their exact expected values on:
    fz2 interp <fixture>
    fz2 run <fixture>
    fz2 build <fixture> -o /tmp/<name> && /tmp/<name>
- The captured minimal repro prints exactly {:a, 11}; no unstable large integer.
- The sequential-match witness has no “materialize direct-only callable”,
  “rematerialize generic callable”, “cannot project captures”, or
  “native executable lowering failed” diagnostic.
- Backend/native facts no longer pair a semantically concrete invoked closure
  with callable(<unknown>/0 captures=[] shapes=[] lanes=[]); the construction
  and its int capture remain recoverable at the call.
- The top-level captured-callable control stays green.
- callsite_dispatch::tests::a_closure_nested_in_a_tuple_is_named_by_the_test
  and a_nested_callables_captures_are_a_question stay green.
- Full lib and fixture matrix pass; fmt and clippy are clean with zero warnings.

comments.text:
STILL RED at fz-kdt.119's head (4ca1dc7e7), as expected -- 119 did not touch it and this ticket still owns it. One symptom MOVED, so the reproducer's error text in this ticket is now stale:

  refnest.fz  (the {tag, f} = box destructure through a forwarding hop)
    base  b32d645ac: 'native executable lowering failed for index 13'
    head  4ca1dc7e7: 'native cannot project captures out of a callable that
                      names no function in Executable(... FunctionId(66) ...)'
  refnest2.fz: unchanged, still fails all three doors.

Same failure, one layer earlier: the callable-identity envelope now reaches the nested position (that is 119's item 3), so the nested callable is named where it used to be widened, and the lowering refuses at capture projection rather than at the end. Neither compiles, so 119's REFNEST acceptance probe stayed unconstructible exactly as this ticket said.

CONSEQUENCE HONOURED: 119's nested-callable separation is gated by UNIT tests at the dispatch layer instead --
  callsite_dispatch::tests::a_closure_nested_in_a_tuple_is_named_by_the_test
  callsite_dispatch::tests::a_nested_callables_captures_are_not_a_question
-- which pin both halves of the law (two callables one tuple deep are two disjoint questions; one callable at two capture layouts is ONE question, joining fz-kdt.127's population). When this ticket lands, those claims want the three-door fixture the probes were meant to be.

RE-TESTED at 29b07acfa (after fz-kdt.127.1 + .2, 2026-09-02): STILL RED, unchanged in kind. refnest.fz: interp correct ({:a, 11} {:a, 30}); native refuses 'native cannot project captures out of a callable that names no function in Executable(... FunctionId(66) ...)' then 'native executable lowering failed for index 13'. refnest2.fz (pattern-destructured): interp 'backend executable 11 function 65 clause 0 failed before entry 0: backend value 0 is unbound'; native same refusal. Neither stage of 127 touched the nested-in-tuple capture projection; the closures here capture nothing, so the forwarder key still erases them to the bare arrow inside the tuple (capture-free literals erase whole), and the refusal is the transport/projection of a callable position INSIDE a tuple through an erased hop. Still this ticket's. Note for whoever picks it up: 127.2's anonymous literal closure[?](caps) also 'names no function' -- a capture-BEARING closure nested in a tuple through a forwarder would meet the same refusal one form later; add that variant to the reproducers.

title: P1: native loses callable identity and captures when invoking a closure projected from a tuple
